package_info.why_malicious: The package is vulnerable to uncontrolled resource consumption (CVE-2021-22119). It allows an attacker to generate an unlimited number of OAuth2 authorization requests per session, which are stored in the session without expiration or size limit. This leads to unbounded memory usage and can result in denial of service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, during OAuth2 authorization request handling

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, during OAuth2 authorization request processing, the code retrieves the current map of authorization requests from the session, inserts a new request keyed by a unique state, and stores the updated map back into the session without enforcing any limit or expiration, resulting in unbounded accumulation of session data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code enables an attacker to store an unlimited number of OAuth2 authorization requests in the session by repeatedly sending requests with unique state values. There are no checks for maximum size or expiration, allowing the session data to grow indefinitely and consume excessive memory.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to enforce a maximum number of stored authorization requests per session and to expire or clean up old or unused requests. The actual implementation lacks these controls, allowing indefinite accumulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate implementations store a single or a small, bounded number of authorization requests per session to track ongoing OAuth2 flows, with proper cleanup after use.
key_indicators: No limit on the number of OAuth2 authorization requests stored per session
No expiration or cleanup mechanism for session-stored authorization requests
Direct storage of user-controlled data (state and authorizationRequest) in session
Session attribute updated on every authorization request without pruning

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends repeated OAuth2 authorization requests to the application, each with a unique state parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Accumulation of OAuth2 authorization requests in the session store.

attack_chain.action: Application stores each authorization request in the session without any limit or expiration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unbounded growth of session data and memory usage.

attack_chain.action: System resources (memory) are exhausted due to the accumulation of abandoned authorization requests.

behavioral_signatures: Unbounded increase in the number of OAuth2 authorization requests stored in session data
Multiple unique OAuth2 state parameters present in a single session
Absence of expiration or cleanup for session-stored authorization requests
Session attribute for authorization requests grows continuously without reduction
network_indicators: High frequency of OAuth2 authorization requests from a single user or IP address
Repeated OAuth2 requests with unique state parameters from the same source
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor session storage for rapid or unbounded growth in the number of OAuth2 authorization requests per session. Set alerts if the count exceeds a reasonable threshold (e.g., more than 5-10 per session) or if there is no evidence of expiration or cleanup over time. Additionally, monitor network traffic for high-frequency OAuth2 authorization requests with unique state parameters originating from the same user or IP address, which may indicate an attempt to exploit the vulnerability.
